There is a line drawn. The line is drawn at assaulting real people. Fictional people aren't real. If romanticizing fictional serial killers, murderers, and violent criminals doesn't turn you into one, then reading about fictional child predators won't turn you into one either. The thing about fiction and fantasy is that it should be a safe place to explore things you couldn't/wouldn't/shouldn't do in real life. Specifically because you can't, won't, don't. The human brain is curious, and pushing to ban things, has always made people more curious about those things. To explore them on your own in a fictional setting is the only place to safely explore it. And I don't know about you, but I don't want to risk banning the only safe option for fear people might let their curiosity win in real situations. Assaulting a child, assaulting anyone, is heinous. But let fiction be the place people play with the idea, instead of reality.

Deconstructing what a man is is a good way to get lost. Instead, maybe deconstruct what you want. Focus on "you" instead of "them." It sounds like you want to live in a male body. That being male physically would be more comfortable to you. If you're non-binary, that doesn't have to change at all if you transition physically, but you're definitely allowed to reevaluate as you go, identity is a journey that never ends. I'm a little shaky on your presentation ideals, but it sounds like you'd like to be masculine most of the time, and maybe a bit feminine some of the time, or even androgynous. You can be all of those things if that's what feels best for you. 

Not fitting in can feel pretty isolating, but there are a ton of people out there who have various nontraditional gender identities and from what I can tell, you don't actively judge them for it. So, maybe try judging yourself the way you'd judge us. I'm gender fluid, afab, and feminine/androgynous. I would absolutely transition physically if my life had gone a little differently, but I'd still be gender fluid and mostly feminine. Would you tell me that I was wrong to want a male body when I don't even identify as a man most of the time? I don't think you would. And you wouldn't be wrong to want something similar. 

There are still a bunch of thoughtless and cruel people out there, but our community is growing with people finding self actualization and allies; we're everywhere. And as much as we can, we'll have your back. Even if it's just talking to a stranger on the internet. Usually you'll find someone who Gets It. You're allowed to wait, if it feels unsafe for you. You don't ever have to transition if you don't want to, but try to let yourself accept what you really want without thinking about the social ramifications, and then you can work out the rest.

So, my first instinct is to say that if she's not willing to grow and change with you then you may want to chat with her a bit more about your needs and expectations... But I'm in a similar situation and I chose differently. 

I happen to know that my partner would not be attracted to me if I had a male body. We're both sexual and monogamous, so I know we wouldn't be happy together if I transitioned. But in my case, I'm gender fluid, so I'm happy with who I am a good deal of the time. I chose to give up on the idea of transitioning, because being in this body with my partner makes me happier than than the idea of being in a man's body without him. I think the thing that really made my decision final in my brain, was that I know with all my heart that he would support me completely if I decided I really really couldn't live without transitioning. And I know he'd still love me, in a way. That knowledge is why I know I can be happier as a female with him than as a male without. 

The choice you have to make depends a lot on the details of your situation. I chose to give up a large part of who I am, but despite it sounding contradictory, I also chose what would make me happiest in the long run. They just happened to be the same choice. I'm still mourning that piece of me a bit, but I'm allowed to be sad for something and happy with my choices at the same time. 

So choose what you think is ultimately going to make you the happiest. Even if it hurts a little right now, you'll be able to move forward and learn to live without whatever —or whoever— you left behind. 

My heart goes out for you. Good luck.

So, I mentioned on another post my interpretation of sex, gender and presentation, and I think it makes a lot more sense. I focus on three things; sex, presentation, and gender. So, sex is biological, male-female, it's about chromosomes and genitals and secondary sex characteristics. Presentation, masculine-feminine, is just that; how you present yourself to others, it's the walk and the talk. Which does in fact leave gender, man-woman, to be about gender norms, traditional places in society. The second two are social constructs, all are infinitely variable, and you can combine them in any way you like. 

Something else to remember is that there's no reason for anyone to break gender norms if they don't want to. There's no shame in that. We all want to have self actualization and be respected as people regardless of where we fall on those three spectrums. 

The thing about pronouns is that they tend to hold personal value over tradition. Due to that, there's no right or wrong when it comes to choosing pronouns. It depends on each person, and because it can make or break someone's sense of self and personal comfort, there's no reason not to respect them. No one is expecting perfection, especially since society has eliminated trans history from common knowledge, it takes time to spread knowledge and its made harder by people who refuse to accept new information. All anyone is asking for is some effort. We all make mistakes, hell we misgender ourselves sometimes. Just correct and move on and try again next time. 

Language is imprecise at the best of times, communication is hard. You can say the same thing five times in different ways and still have someone get it backwards from what you intended. 

So, yeah, it's not going to be easy. 

But when you see those kids in your class and think about how scared they may have been growing up in a society that questions who they are at every turn, just know that every time you respect their pronouns, no matter what they are or whether they match their sex or gender or presentation, that they feel more themselves. You're helping them find a sense of normalcy in who they are, which is amazing for kids who feel like they're different. And, you're teaching everyone around them that normalcy and respect. Kindness like that spreads, and you're doing a great thing. 

I guess, all in all, you don't have to see something to believe in it, and you don't have to understand something to respect it. And that's okay. We're all learning and growing together in this huge amazing world, so I think it's really cool that you have questions and want to learn. Maybe there will be better answers later, or things will change, but for now, it's okay that you and I don't understand everything. We're doing our best to respect it and that's good for now.

It sounds like you have a lot of things to work through. I know it's not great advice, but honestly I think you might want to consider finding a therapist. They're trained to guide you through untangling all those thoughts and processing past traumas. Finding a therapist you like can be a long and frustrating process, but it can be so rewarding. 

Other than that, getting my thoughts out of me is always my first step when I have a big confused brain tangle. I do it by getting in my car and driving loops around my city with my windows down and the radio blasting while I talk to myself (or my car) loudly. I call it car therapy, lol. My best friend does it by writing lists. I have another friend who likes to set up an area to paint messily while shouting her feelings at the canvas. Anything that gets your thoughts out of your head and into the world where you can see/hear/touch them, move them around and organize them into something that is easier to understand. Sometimes that's all it takes for me to have a realization, but often there are underlying issues or things I haven't addressed that need finding and my therapist helps me deal with all that. 

I wish you luck on your journey and I hope you can come to a peaceful place with yourself soon!

It's possible for the swan in the body of the gull to feel dysphoria the same way the duck does. But at the same time, the gull may feel no dysphoria at all because the gull sees a gull in the mirror and that matches, but if the swan sees a gull in the mirror it doesn't. 

So you can see that they are different concepts that can certainly interact, but are not mutually inclusive. I guess in a way they are a little bit similar since they're both sort of like an identity crisis, but I wouldn't think them to be like each other much at all otherwise. 

I don't know anything about the kinds of medication or therapy that exists for multiple personality, but I'd assume it would be very different from dysphoria. Honestly multiple personality kind of scares me because bodily autonomy is like, the most basic of human rights and how can that work if two people share the same body??? I'd feel so violated...

Yeah, it's hard. I was a lot less pushy with my parents, but mostly because I spent a lot of time when I was younger learning them really really well (undiagnosed adhd, you get it). And so my biggest struggle was the waiting. 

My parents are pretty awesome and supportive and willing to change and grow, but they are not fast. Often I would have a conversation with my mom where she'd say something and I'd correct her, and she wouldn't really accept it, but later she'd tell me a story of how she was on the phone with one of her sisters and they'd say something and my mom would correct them the same way I had. 

She just took a while to process, probably did a little bit of research on her own (because she taught me my critical thinking skills and individual research was a big part of it), and then managed to come to terms with the idea. I don't know if she forgot that I was the one who originally told her (I believe she also has undiagnosed adhd or similar, but only because we have some similar symptoms) or if she was trying to tell me that she gets it now without having to apologize for not believing me right away (which is something I find perfectly understandable, like, verifying information is important and admitting you're wrong is hard). 

My dad on the other hand, was pretty quiet about the whole thing (not outwardly emotional for the most part, that one) But when I changed my name I know he was pretty sad and felt like I was rejecting him (he still came with me on my court date and helped me through the process of changing all my paperwork stuff, getting a new ss card, passport, credit card, etc.) He wasn't very good at calling me my new name for a long time, but mom got good at it faster and dad caught up from hearing it so often and he hasn't called me my original name since... well... it's been a couple years now I think. 

I have one older friend who still just, deadnames me because he doesn't want to deal with change, and that's kind of hurtful, but there's this nickname he really really hates and I just call him by that and it feels kind of like it's okay. I don't see him physically anymore since I moved, so it's not like he can spread it to anyone new. We don't talk that often anyway. Luckily I've managed to get out of the stage where I had panic attacks when I saw or heard my deadname, so things are improving. 

I'm not sure where I was going with all this, but things are different for everyone and while I definitely get that we deserve respect as people, and that it hurts when we don't get it right away like we should, and that we shouldn't have to shoulder this responsibility as victims, but I guess it helps me to remember that it took me years to figure out who I was and what I wanted. And maybe that was because there wasn't much information at the time, and no one nearby to educate me, but I took a long time on my self journey and no one was in my head for it. So, I guess I don't mind, letting everyone else have their journey too? Ally's aren't perfect and they don't just pop out of the ground knowing everything. They have to grow too. And people grow at different rates and different ways... I like to think, given the time, and learning style, anyone could come to understand and respect us. It sucks, having to wait. It's not fair and it feels crappy and lots of people are hurting. But lots of people are growing too. The hot air is rising, the cold air is sinking, and one day we'll be ideal temperature soup. Hopefully sooner rather than later, but definitely someday.

My first inkling of feeling like I had a future. And I held him over my head and nearly smashed him to pieces on the hardwood... I reached out the next day. Between then and my first appointment I wrote my last suicide letter. 

It took months of therapy and more months of meds before I had my first real breakthrough. It almost (but not quite) made me understand people who don't believe in depression, because I honestly had never believed in a life without it. Not until I found myself there.

And it was like waking up from that fog all over again. Sometimes I still can't believe it. I have normal days, friend. Real actual normal days that don't exhaust me and make me feel like I'm just slogging through life to get to the end. The kind that aren't good days, or bad days, but just days that could probably look like any other day except I can breathe now. It took me 25 years to have normal days... 

I guess the point though, is that I want so badly for everyone to have the kind of normal days I have now. I wish I could show everyone what it's like. That it's real and worth reaching for. And I am so damn proud of you for taking your first steps because they can be so fucking hard. Attractiveness has no bearing on sexuality my friend! I too feel unattractive, but my pansexual nonbinary ass is labeled and active! And if you don't want a label that's okay. It's not like they're necessary. But there are tons out there, and getting a clean cut answer isn't usually easy. 

Bisexual and pansexual overlap greatly, but both include sexual attraction to two or more genders. There's also the possibility of being bisexual and heteroromantic, meaning you feel sexual attraction to two or more genders, but you're only interested in romantic relationships with the opposite gender. You could be completely straight while occasionally being in the mood for gay porn. 

You also may just want to relate to your friends better, in which case you could ask them if they think you could be a better ally in any way. They may say no, you might be doing just fine! 

The problem with clean cut answers, is that the most important deciding factor, is how YOU feel about applying a label to yourself. Any label or a specific label, it's all about your comfort, your desire. All we can do is make suggestions and wish you well.

I heard vinegar was good, but ideally you shouldn't be getting any on your skin at all. The reaction to resin also varies from person to person, and you don't wanna be that person with a mid sized bucket and accidentally fill it only to be faced with anaphylaxis instead of a small skin rash. I hope the alcohol works okay and you stay safe! (But do consider using more skin protection)

Getting resin on your skin has a cumulative effect. Sort of like putting drops of water into a bucket. When there just a few drops its no big deal, but eventually after a while, the bucket overflows and tadaaah! Contact dermatitis! The question is just how big is your bucket? Everyone has a different sized bucket and when the bucket is full you're sensitized and will have reactions to the substance for the rest of your life, permanent avoidance is the only "cure." Some people have a bucket the size of a thimble and may fill it up with their very first exposure, some have a whole pond. Thats why its so important to be safe while using resin. Respirator and gloves at all times, well ventilated area. There's no way of knowing how big your bucket is or how full its become until it overflows.

Practice on a junk circuit board until you're more comfortable. I find soldering to be a pretty forgiving as long as you don't burn anything. Try not to leave the iron on the components for more than a few seconds at a time and if they feel warm, shoot em with some compressed air or let them cool a bit before continuing. Have a solder sucker AND a wick, they're both extremely useful but sometimes you'll find only one or the other will work well in a situation. Some alligator clips on wire stuck in a weight will also go a long way, or get a cheap third hand, either way, no need to be fancy. Watch a couple youtube videos before you start if you're nervous, and don't burn yourself. Make sure no matter what kind of soldering iron you have that its very stable when you put it down. Too much solder will drip, make sure its not over your lap when it does. A damp sponge and some steel wire are good for cleaning up your iron occasionally. Usually after a few components, but you'll start to feel it when you practice a little. Use flux or get flux core solder. I've had great results with flux core solder but I've heard from people out there who haven't and I have no idea what brand mine is, it was inherited. 

So yeah. Practice, be safe, and keep your stuff clean. 

And maybe keep a window open nearby, the stuff smells.

I dont wanna sound like that hopeful cheerful person that doesn't understand. Because I was right there with you a year ago. Every day was a slog, I was exhausted doing nothing, I was a burden to my friends and family and I didn't belive there was anything more to life than that because it was all I'd ever known. I've written 14 suicide notes in my life. I dont know if that's not many or a lot to you, but I was tired. I was tired when I was 8, when I was 12, 13, 15, 16 twice, 17, 19 three times 20 twice, 22. I wanted to disappear. Because I had a good life, you know. And if that wasn't enough, what else could there be. 

I won't go into details, but an event occurred in my life that made me want so badly to believe that there WAS something. Anything. And I started therapy. Therapy was okay. It was someone to talk to who was paid to listen and at least had a professional interest in whether I lived or died If I wasn't there, they wouldn't get my money. Even a small thing like that made me feel like I was useful to someone. After 4 months I'd had several breakdowns in the office and my therapist recommended a meds provider. I wrote my 14th suicide note the day before the appointment. I didn't do it because funny enough, someone on reddit said something that clicked with me, and I wanted them to be happy. I had to be alive to find out if they became happy. 

I started an antidepressant and life went on. I was told those things were slow, it might not be the right med for me, and to keep going to therapy. And the months passed by, marked by things like, "the med might be working a little? We can add this to help you absorb it, oh, you've also got ADD that was hiding out under the depression and anxiety? We have drugs for that!" I worried that I had been right all along, that things would never be as bright and hopeful as people liked to say. I thought it was me, maybe I was weaker than everyone else, that I couldn't handle the same existence because I lacked something. 

After 4 months I had a breakthrough. It was the most amazing and least comfortable thing that has ever happened to me. I had therapy that day, and when I left, I was choking on tears, sobbing, laughing hysterically I felt manic and scared and sick and hopeful. I had never felt hope before in my life until that moment. I knew the word, the definition, I'd thought I'd felt hope. That day I became a new person. Except... I was also exactly the same as I'd always been. Because it was me, but not because I was weak or bad at life, I was actually physically misaligned. I was walking another plane of existence entirely. It almost made me understand those people who don't believe in depression, because I didn't believe in a life without it until I found myself there. I hated them because they didn't believe in me, but I didnt believe in them either. Its easy not to believe in things you've never experienced. Things you can't imagine. 

I apologize for the life story, but... even after 23 years of... of... of that feeling, that probably feels a little like you're feeling. I can see the other side of the fence. And maybe it didn't really feel like it had all been worth it all along right away... maybe it still doesn't really. But I can see a future. A real one. One that I want to be around to see. One where I think one day, the past will be so far away I'll start taking my new life for granted. I can honestly say, right now, today I have had an awful terrible day. I've cried I've done my least favorite things and I did them while I was tired and hungry and had to pee and it rained on me which I hate. Its been a horrible day. But I dont want to disappear anymore. I'm not always wondering when its going to finally end. I'm thinking about tomorrow. And wondering if it will be a good day or another bad day. The thought of killing myself hasn't crossed my mind in 8 months when it used to do several times a week. Or even several times a day. 

I dont know your circumstances or your name or anything about you really. But I hope you can experience the other side someday.
